ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: this case is going to a human reviewer, and no money moves today. The SGD 4.50 cancellation fee is held — neither refunded to the rider nor released to the driver — while the review is pending.

Why. POL-NS-09(c) requires escalation where the rider's and the driver's profiles together show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same two people in the trailing 90 days. Each of your profiles carries 2 such disputes (rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2; driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2). Two meets the clause's '2 or more' threshold, so the automated pipeline must stop here. This is a repeat pattern that one trip's record cannot fairly judge, in either direction, so I make no overall finding of fault.

What the trip record itself shows. The driver's 'arrived' event is at 13:03:54; the GPS trace places the driver at the pickup point from 13:03:54 and holds him there for a continuous 390 seconds; the free waiting period in force for this trip was 180 seconds; the trip was ended by the driver at 13:10:24 with the reason RIDER_NO_SHOW. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold and the POL-NS-02 arrival test passes. The rider's own device track sits about 764 m from the pin (min 760.03 m, max 767.76 m), outside the 100 m presence radius for this STANDARD zone; the only chat message on the trip is the driver's 'im here' at 13:04:24, so POL-NS-04 (rider contact unanswered) cannot apply because the rider sent no locating message; POL-NS-03 (wrong entrance) does not apply because the driver was inside the arrival radius, not outside it; POL-NS-05 is not triggered (the driver was stationary at the pin at the marker); and POL-NS-06 shows no shortfall (390 s measured against the 180 s minimum). The fare line of SGD 4.50 matches the fee in force for this trip, so there is no POL-NS-08 fare defect, and every artifact I used carries full weight 1.0.

Had the case stopped there, the fee would have stood and the driver would have been paid 80 percent of it, SGD 3.60, under POL-NS-07 — the anti-farming test does not trip, because driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 against 110 completed trips in 30 days (the tests are 4 or more, and a rate above 0.08).

The rider's statement that this is 'the third time' is not borne out: the record shows 2 disputes between this pair, not 3. But 2 is already at the escalation threshold, so that point does not change the outcome.

The open question for the reviewer: whether the repeated no-show disputes between this rider and this driver show a rider who repeatedly fails to appear (in which case the SGD 4.50 fee stands and SGD 3.60 is paid to the driver under POL-NS-07), or repeated mis-cancellation by the driver (in which case the fee is refunded to the rider), or a mix of both.

A note on the profile material: lifetime counters such as prior_no_show_flags were treated as context only and were not used as a ground, as POL-GEN-01 requires.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
